Once created, the webhook starts receiving deliveries for its subscribed event_types (or every event type, if event_types is omitted). destination_config's required fields depend on destination_type — see the examples below for the exact shape expected by each of the five supported destinations (generic, slack, microsoft_teams, pagerduty, github).

slack.description: Posts alert events to a Slack channel via an Incoming Webhook URL. webhook_url must be hosted on hooks.slack.com.

microsoft_teams.description: Posts alert events to a Teams channel as an Adaptive Card via a Teams Workflows (Power Automate) webhook URL, hosted on *.logic.azure.com or *.api.powerplatform.com. Classic Office 365 connector URLs are rejected.

pagerduty.description: Triggers a PagerDuty incident via an Events API v2 integration's routing_key.

github.description: Opens a GitHub issue in the given repo for each subscribed event, authenticated with a fine-grained personal access token.

generic.description: Posts the raw event payload to any HTTPS URL you control. api_version is required for this destination type since there is no fixed integration format to infer it from.

get.summary: List subscribable webhook event types with sample payloads

Lets a client render an accurate payload preview per event type instead of hardcoding the list and a single generic example.

get.summary: Public JWKS of webhook signing keys
get.description: Returns the platform's current and recently-retired Ed25519 public keys, in JWK format, so webhook consumers can verify the X-Skaletek-Signature header on incoming deliveries. Unauthenticated and safe to call from a consumer's own backend — no tenant context is needed since signing keys are global to the platform, not per-tenant. Consumers should look up the key by the "kid" in the signature header rather than assuming a single fixed key, since keys rotate periodically and old ones stay valid for a grace period.

patch.description: Updates one or more fields of an existing webhook. Only the fields present in the request body are changed. destination_config is replaced wholesale when provided (not deep-merged), so include every key it should end up with. destination_type itself cannot be changed — delete this webhook and create a new one to switch destinations.

delete.description: Permanently removes the webhook and stops all future deliveries to it. Past delivery history is not retained after deletion. This cannot be undone — recreate the webhook (a new id, no history) if deleted by mistake.

post.summary: Activate a paused webhook

Reactivating after a circuit-breaker pause does not retry the deliveries that were skipped while paused; only new events going forward will be delivered. Returns 409 if the webhook is already active.

post.summary: Deactivate (pause) a webhook
post.description: Pauses a webhook so no further deliveries are attempted until it is reactivated (paused_reason is set to "user"). Useful while rotating a destination's credentials or debugging integration issues, without losing the webhook's configuration or delivery history. Returns 409 if the webhook is already paused.

Rate-limited per webhook to prevent abuse (see the 429 response).

post.summary: Invite someone outside the tenant to one task
post.description:
Issues a link scoped to a single task. The invited party sees that task and nothing else of the case, so keep tasks narrow: a supplier contact asked for a tax form must not be handed the ownership file.

Issuing revokes the task's previous links, so there is only ever one way in. The token is returned once and cannot be recovered; reissue if it is lost. Only counterparty roles can be invited, not the tenant's own staff.

get.summary: Open an invited task
get.description:
The counterparty entry point. No account and no bearer token: the link itself is the credential, and it answers for one task only.

An unknown, expired or revoked link all return the same 401, so the response never says whether a token existed.

post.summary: Decide a case
post.description:
Records a reviewer's conclusion on the case's frozen version. The graph must be frozen first, so the decision names the exact evidence it was made on.

When the template sets require_four_eyes the decision waits: the case moves to pending_review and a different reviewer must confirm it. With four-eyes off it takes effect at once. Either way the outcome sets the kyb:* label on the counterparty.

A restricted outcome must name at least one condition, since a restriction nothing can act on is not a decision.

value.rationale: Ownership corroborated against the RCCM extract; no screening hits.
PEP among the beneficial owners; onboarding under EDD.

409.description: The case is closed, has no frozen version, or already has a decision pending

post.summary: Confirm a decision as the second reviewer
post.description: Applies the decision awaiting confirmation. The confirmer must be a different person to the one who proposed it, which is enforced in the write itself, so two requests cannot both win.

403.description: You proposed this decision, so it still needs a second reviewer

409.description: Already confirmed or replaced

Everything the KYB tab on an entity profile needs in one call: for each relationship type the case status, its latest version with the computed ownership results, the decision in force, outstanding task counts and what is holding it up. The kyb:* label comes from GET /entities/{entityId} with the entity's other labels.

An organization with no KYB case returns an empty list rather than a 404.

label_value.description: The screening:* label applied to the entity when a match carrying this topic is confirmed. Absent when the topic drives no label.

WebhookDestinationType.description: Where delivery payloads are sent. Determines which fields destination_config must contain: generic requires "url" (any HTTPS endpoint) and a top-level api_version; slack and microsoft_teams require "webhook_url" (Slack's must be hosted on hooks.slack.com; Teams' must be a Workflows / Power Automate webhook URL on *.logic.azure.com or *.api.powerplatform.com); pagerduty requires "routing_key"; github requires "repo" and "token".

WebhookRetryPolicy.description: How failed deliveries are retried before being marked dead_letter.

max_retries.description: Number of retry attempts after the initial delivery fails, before giving up (dead_letter).

backoff.description: exponential doubles the delay after each failed attempt; fixed retries at a constant interval.

initial_delay_ms.description: Delay before the first retry, in milliseconds. Subsequent delays depend on backoff.

WebhookStatus.description: active webhooks receive deliveries normally. paused webhooks are skipped — either because a user paused them, or because the circuit breaker tripped after too many consecutive failures (see paused_reason).

WebhookPausedReason.description: Why a webhook is currently paused. "user" means someone called deactivateWebhook explicitly; "circuit_breaker" means the platform paused it automatically after consecutive_failures crossed the failure threshold, to stop retrying a destination that is consistently rejecting deliveries.

WebhookDeliveryStatus.description: Outcome of one delivery attempt. pending means the attempt hasn't completed yet; success means the destination returned a 2xx; failed means it will be retried per retry_policy; dead_letter means retries were exhausted and the delivery was given up on; skipped means no HTTP call was made (the webhook was paused, or the payload exceeded the 1 MB cap); discarded means an operator removed a dead_letter delivery from the dead letter queue without retrying it.

Webhook.description: A registered webhook destination and its delivery health for the caller's tenant.

destination_config.description: Destination-specific settings; shape depends on destination_type (see WebhookDestinationType). Secrets such as routing_key or token are returned masked (e.g. "sk-...abcd").

api_version.description: Payload schema version to send. Required for generic destinations; ignored for the built-in integrations (Slack, Teams, PagerDuty, GitHub), which have a fixed payload shape.

event_types.description: Event types this webhook is subscribed to (e.g. "alert.created"). Null subscribes to all event types except opt-in ones (see WebhookEventType.opt_in), which must be listed explicitly.

consecutive_failures.description: Number of delivery attempts that have failed in a row since the last success. Resets to 0 on the next successful delivery; crossing the platform's failure threshold pauses the webhook with paused_reason=circuit_breaker.

delivered_count.description: Lifetime count of deliveries that received a successful (2xx) response.

failed_count.description: Lifetime count of deliveries that ended in failed or dead_letter.

created_by.description: User who created this webhook, if created via the API by a signed-in user rather than provisioned by the system.

updated_by.description: User who last modified this webhook's configuration.

WebhookListResponse.description: Paginated list of webhooks registered for the caller's tenant.

CreateWebhookRequest.description: Registers a new webhook destination. destination_config's required fields depend on destination_type — see WebhookDestinationType for the per-destination shape. The example below is for a Slack Incoming Webhook; see the createWebhook operation description for an example per destination type.

destination_config.description: Destination-specific settings; required fields depend on destination_type (see WebhookDestinationType).

api_version.description: Payload schema version to send. Required when destination_type is generic; ignored for the built-in integrations.

event_types.description: Event types to subscribe to (e.g. "alert.created"). Omit or leave null to receive every event type except opt-in ones (e.g. event.created), which must be listed explicitly.

WebhookEventType.description: One subscribable event type, its subscription category (used to group the picker in the webhook creation UI), and a realistic sample of the "data" field a delivery for this event type carries — the same sample the test-delivery endpoint uses for this event_type.

event_type.description: Value to pass in event_types when creating/updating a webhook, or as TestWebhookRequest.event_type.

category.description: Grouping label for the subscription picker UI (e.g. "Alerts", "Events", "Screening", "Rules", "Reports").

implemented.description: False for event types the frontend already advertises but the platform does not emit yet — sample_data is a plausible placeholder for these, not a guarantee of the eventual real shape. True event types are emitted in production exactly as shown here.

opt_in.description: True for high-volume event types (e.g. event.created) that are only delivered to webhooks listing them explicitly in event_types; a webhook subscribed to all event types (event_types null) does not receive them.

sample_data.description: Sample of the envelope's "data" field for this event_type — identical to what POST /webhooks/{webhookId}/test produces for the same event_type.

description.en: An alert is created by a rule match.
description.fr: Une alerte est créée suite à la correspondance d'une règle.

alert.title: Sender transferred to 3 or more distinct receivers within 24h

WebhookVerificationKeysResponse.description: Public Ed25519 verification keys used by webhook consumers to verify X-Skaletek-Signature.

keys.description: Active signing key and recently retired keys retained during the verification grace period.

kid.description: Key identifier referenced by the kid field in X-Skaletek-Signature.

kty.description: JWK key type. Always OKP for Ed25519 keys.

UpdateWebhookRequest.description: Partial update of an existing webhook's configuration. Only the fields present are changed; destination_type cannot be changed after creation — delete and recreate the webhook instead.

destination_config.description: Destination-specific settings to replace. Provide the full destination_config, not just the changed keys — this is a full replacement of the object, not a deep merge.

api_version.description: Payload schema version to send. Only meaningful when destination_type is generic.

event_types.description: Event types to subscribe to. Omit to leave unchanged; set to null to subscribe to all event types.

WebhookSignatureMode.description: Which signature to send with a test delivery's X-Skaletek-Signature header, so consumers can exercise their signature-verification code against both a valid and an intentionally broken signature. valid signs normally; invalid sends a signature that will fail verification; stale signs with a retired (but still grace-period-valid) signing key.

WebhookDelivery.description: One attempt to deliver an event payload to a webhook's destination.

event_type.description: The event that triggered this delivery, e.g. "alert.created". "webhook.test" for deliveries sent via the test endpoint.

http_status.description: HTTP status code returned by the destination, if the request was sent.

latency_ms.description: Round-trip time of the delivery attempt, in milliseconds.

attempt_count.description: How many attempts (including this one) have been made for this logical delivery, per retry_policy.

response_excerpt.description: First part of the destination's response body, truncated, kept for debugging failed deliveries.

error.description: Human-readable failure reason when status is failed or dead_letter (e.g. a timeout or connection error).

is_test.description: True if this delivery was triggered via the testWebhook endpoint rather than a real platform event.

actor_type.description: Kind of actor whose action produced the underlying event (e.g. "user", "system", "rule").

display_name.description: Resolved actor display name when actor_type is user.

source_type.description: Kind of platform resource that generated the event, e.g. "alert" or "entity".

source_id.description: ID of the platform resource referenced by source_type.

delivered_at.description: When the destination accepted the delivery (status became success). Null while pending or if it never succeeded.

WebhookDeliveryListResponse.description: Paginated delivery history for one webhook, most recent first.

WebhookDeliveryAttempt.description: One HTTP attempt made for a delivery.

WebhookDeliveryDetailResponse.description: A delivery with the exact envelope that was (or will be) sent and every attempt made so far — the inspect view of the dead letter queue.

payload.description: The generic delivery envelope (id, event_type, api_version, created_at, test, data). Native destinations receive it rendered into their own format.

TestWebhookRequest.description: Sends a synthetic delivery so integrators can verify their endpoint and signature-verification logic without waiting for a real platform event.

event_type.description: Event type to simulate in the test payload. Defaults to "webhook.test" if omitted.

RotateWebhookCredentialRequest.description: Replaces the secret credential in a webhook's destination_config (PagerDuty's routing_key or GitHub's token) without touching the rest of the configuration — use this instead of updateWebhook when only the secret changed, e.g. after regenerating it at the destination. The previous credential remains usable for 24 hours: if the destination rejects the new one during that window, the delivery is retried with the previous one.

destination_config.description: Partial destination config containing only the new routing_key (pagerduty) or token (github).

entry_type.description: For kind=country/value, one of country, string, phone, email, iban, url, product_ref, keyword. For kind=entity, a FollowTheMoney schema name (Person, Company, ...) or "*" for mixed schemas.

index_version.description: Monotonic dataset version reported by the screening backend.

collections.description: Active collections this list is a direct member of. Returned on the list detail (GET /lists/{listId}) for entity-kind lists only.

created_at.description: Null for platform datasets published directly in the screening backend.

entry_type.description: For kind=country/value, one of country, string, phone, email, iban, url, product_ref, keyword. For kind=entity, a FollowTheMoney schema name (Person, Company, ...) or "*" (defaults to "*" when omitted).

list_id.description: The dataset's id in the list catalog (GET /lists).

value.description: Canonical value; country lists always return alpha-2.

values.description: Raw values; country lists accept ISO alpha-2 or alpha-3 codes.

effective_from.description: Applied to every entry; defaults to now.

errors.description: One item per rejected value — its index in `values`, the value, and a code.

ManagedListIndexStatusResponse.description: Index state of an entity-kind list's dataset (SPEC 3.12.6): dataset version and indexed entity count as reported by the screening backend, next to the platform's own per-entry sync counters.

entry_count.description: Active entity entries held by the platform.

indexed_entry_count.description: Entities the dataset reports as indexed.

indexed_at.description: Last dataset change reported by the screening backend.

type.description: `list` for an entity-kind list, `collection` for a nested collection, `unknown` when the key no longer resolves to either.

id.description: The list's id in the catalog (GET /lists); absent for nested collections.

entry_count.description: Active entity entries; absent for nested collections.

ManagedListCollection.description: A named grouping of entity-kind lists and/or nested collections (SPEC 3.12.5), resolved to a flattened yente collection at screening time. Backed by yente's own collection store — skalemon-api adds authz, audit, and entity-only/acyclic membership validation on top rather than persisting a separate copy.

members.description: Dataset or collection keys enabled in this collection.

member_details.description: The same members as `members`, resolved to their list or collection metadata.

members.description: The collection's full desired member set (replaces the current one).

KybRelationshipType.description: Why the tenant deals with this counterparty.

KybStage.description: A canonical KYB stage. Templates enable or disable stages; order is fixed.

version.description: Assigned on activation. Null while the template is a draft.

cdd_territory.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code of the territory whose CDD rules apply.

aml_ownership_threshold.description: Ownership percentage at or above which a natural person is an AML beneficial owner.

sanctions_ownership_threshold.description: Aggregated ownership percentage at or above which sanctions ownership applies.

collect_aml_bo.description: Turning this off is a deliberate choice, not a missing graph.

case_count.description: Live cases opened on this template.

aml_ownership_threshold.description: Decimal percentage, greater than 0 and at most 100. Defaults to 25.

sanctions_ownership_threshold.description: Decimal percentage, greater than 0 and at most 100. Defaults to 50.

n.description: Version number within the case, starting at 1.

computed.description: Graph computation output, written on freeze.

KybNodeKind.description: Whether this party is a company or a natural person.

KybPartySummary.description: Enough of a party to name it in a list without a second call.

display_name.description: Human-readable label taken from the party's profile.

KybRepresentative.description: Who to deal with at the counterparty.

entity_id.description: The counterparty organization. KYB graph nodes are platform entities.

KybOrganizationDeclaration.description: Resolves an existing organization by identifier or creates one. Used when the caller does not already hold an entity id.

identifier_field.description: Dot path of the identifying field, e.g. registration_number or tax_id.

profile.description: Declared organization attributes, e.g. legal_name, jurisdiction.

CreateKybCaseRequest.description: Supply exactly one of entity_id or organization. Supplying both, or neither, is a validation error.

display_name.description: Human-readable label taken from the party's profile.

screenable.description: Only screenable parties block a freeze.

last_run_id.description: The run behind these counts, to open it in screening.

pending_matches.description: Matches still awaiting a disposition. Same as the pending disposition count.

dispositions.description: Per-disposition match counts on this party's last run.

labels.description: Currently active screening:* labels on this party.

outstanding.description: Screenable parties with no screening yet. Freeze is blocked while above zero.

dispositions.description: Per-disposition match counts across every party in the graph.

ScreenKybGraphRequest.description: Names the corpus to screen the graph against. There is no tenant-level corpus setting, so the caller picks one as manual screening does.

KybEdgeType.description: How one party relates to another.

KybControlBasis.description: How a party controls a company without owning it.

source.description: Who declared this edge, e.g. user:<id>.

warning_codes.description: FIELD_EDITED when a human overrode what was extracted.

total.description: Decimal percentage the declared ordinary shares add up to.

ownership_sums.description: Declared ordinary shares in each party, as a percentage. A party whose total is not 100 cannot be frozen.

KybDeclaredNode.description: A party in the declared graph. Supply either entity_id for a party that already exists, or identifier_field and identifier_value to resolve or create one.

ref.description: The caller's own handle for this node, used to wire up edges in this request.

identifier_field.description: Dot path of the identifying field, e.g. registration_number or full_name.

profile.description: Declared attributes for this party, e.g. legal_name.

KybDeclaredEdgeInput.description: One relationship. percentage is required on owns and rejected on directs and signs_for. A controls edge needs either a percentage or a control_basis, so control without ownership is always explained.

to_ref.description: The party being owned or controlled.

role_title.description: What a director is called, e.g. Executive Director. Only on a directs edge.

KybFieldInput.description: One declared value. submitted is what a human confirmed; extracted is what a registry or document said. At least one is required, and when they differ the field is flagged FIELD_EDITED.

ReplaceKybGraphRequest.description: The whole declared graph for the case's draft version. Edges are replaced rather than merged, so repeating a request leaves the same state.

KybPartyRole.description: Who a task is addressed to. Drives least privilege: a supplier contact asked for a tax form must not be shown the ownership file.

KybBlockerCode.description:
Why a task cannot move, from a closed list so the client can translate it and rules can branch on it. Required when blocking a task and rejected otherwise. The prose belongs in the change reason, not here.

Waiting on someone: awaiting_counterparty, awaiting_third_party (which one is in fulfilment), awaiting_identity_check, internal_review. The party we asked cannot help: counterparty_cannot_supply, wrong_party. Something arrived but is not usable: document_expired, document_illegible, document_wrong_class, document_not_certified. The source is the problem: registry_unavailable is worth retrying, no_registry_coverage means escalating to another rung.

KybFulfilment.description: The rung of the escalation ladder expected to produce the evidence. Recorded per task because the ladder we climbed is what an examiner reads.

entity_id.description: The party the task is about. Null when they are not known yet.

KybTaskCounts.description: Outstanding tasks by status. Statuses with no tasks are omitted.

entity_id.description: The party this task is about. Required for an identity task.

UpdateKybTaskRequest.description: Only the fields present are changed. Clearing a due date or an assignee uses its own flag, because an omitted field and a null one look the same once decoded. Status moves through its own endpoint.

clear_due_at.description: Remove the due date. Cannot be sent together with due_at.

clear_assignee.description: Unassign the task. Cannot be sent together with assigned_user_id.

reason.description: The human detail behind the code, kept on the task's timeline.

KybActorType.description: What kind of caller made the change.

profile.description: Declared organization attributes to merge, e.g. legal_name, legal_form, address. Only the fields sent are changed.

KybActivityEntry.description: One thing that happened to a case, newest first in the listing.

changes.description: What the action recorded, e.g. the statuses moved between.

KybDocumentClass.description: What a document is. Closed so required-document checklists and the operator UI can rely on it. 'other' is for anything a party sends that does not fit, and checklists must not count it.

task_id.description: The task this document answers, when it answers one.

content_type.description: Inferred from the filename, since direct uploads misreport it.

sha256.description: Hashed by the server from the stored object, not supplied by the client.

issued_at.description: The date the document itself carries. No freshness rule is applied.

source.description: Who or what produced it, same vocabulary as a declared field's source.

extraction.description: Structured fields read off the document. Nothing writes this yet.

KybDocumentCounts.description: Documents held per class. Classes with none are omitted.

file_ref.description: The file_ref handed back by the upload-url call.

task_id.description: The task this answers. Must belong to the same case.

KybDocumentUploadResponse.description: Upload the file straight to upload_url, then register it with POST /kyb/cases/{caseId}/documents using the file_ref. The object is not evidence until it is registered.

KybInvite.description: An operator's view of a link handed to one party. Tokens are never returned here.

contact_redacted.description: Enough to recognise who was invited. The address itself is not kept.

accepted_at.description: When the link was first opened. Null means it never was.

task_id.description: The task to hand out. Must belong to this case and to a counterparty role.

contact.description: Email or phone number. Hashed on arrival and kept only in redacted form, so pass it again if you reissue. Optional, because the link is often delivered by other means.

locale.description: The language the invited party sees.

IssuedKybInvite.description: The token is shown once and cannot be recovered. Deliver it to the invited party; the link is /kyb/counterparty/tasks/{token}.

CounterpartyKybDocument.description: A document the invited party supplied. No provenance or hashes.

CounterpartyKybTask.description: Everything an invited party may see. Deliberately narrow: the task they were asked to do, and what they have already supplied for it. It carries no case id, no company details, no other tasks and no ownership data, because an invite answers for one task only.

locale.description: The language this request was sent in.

documents.description: What has been supplied for this task so far.

CounterpartyAddDocumentRequest.description: The task and the case come from the link, never from this body, so a document can only ever land on the task that was asked for.

KybDecisionOutcome.description: What the reviewer concluded about the counterparty.

KybDecisionCondition.description: A term attached to a restricted relationship, for rules to act on. Restricting the products or the spend a counterparty may transact, or recording that enhanced due diligence is still outstanding.

conditions.description: Required for a restricted outcome, rejected for any other.

KybDecisionState.description: pending_confirmation means four-eyes is on and a second reviewer is awaited. superseded means a later decision replaced it before it took effect.

version_id.description: The frozen version this decision was made on.

confirmed_by.description: The second reviewer. Always a different person to decided_by.

EntityKybBlocker.description: Why a case is held up — which party, which task, and copy to localise.

entity_id.description: Which party, so several blocked directors are tellable apart. Null when the task does not name one yet.

EntityKyb.description: The KYB tab on an organization's profile. An organization can hold one case per relationship type, so this is a list. The kyb:* label is not repeated here: GET /entities/{entityId} already returns the entity's labels.

KybFormTemplateSummary.description: A questionnaire without its schema. The questions and the compiled snapshot are large, so they come from GET /kyb/form-templates/{id}.

KybFormSection.description: An ordered group of question names, for the renderer.

properties.description: A JSON Schema object of questions, with the same x-skaletek extensions event templates use. x-skaletek-rename, x-skaletek-omit and x-skaletek-computed are not supported on a form yet and are rejected rather than quietly ignored.

version.description: Assigned on activation. Null while a draft.

properties.description: The questions as the designer wrote them.

compiled_schema.description: The snapshot taken on activation. Answers are checked against this, so editing a draft later cannot change what an answered form meant.

form_template_id.description: The exact form version asked for. Activating a newer version of the same questionnaire leaves this binding, and any open case, alone.

form_slug.description: The questionnaire this asks for, across all its versions.

party_id.description: The declared party this answer is about. Null when the form is answered once for the case rather than per party.

version_id.description: The case version this answer was given on.

version_n.description: That version's number within the case, starting at 1.

is_current_version.description: False when the answer came from an earlier version of the case, which happens once a new draft is opened.

KybCaseForm.description: A form a case asks for, with each party's latest answer.

responses.description: The latest answer from each party that has answered, newest first per party. Empty when nobody has.

party_id.description: The declared party these answers are about, for a form asked of a role that several parties hold. Leave it out to answer once for the case. Must be a party this case declared.

payload.description: The answers, checked against the form's compiled snapshot. Computed questions are filled in by the server and rejected if sent.

ExplainStatusParam.name: status
ExplainStatusParam.description: Keep runs that ended in one of these statuses.

ExplainOutcomeParam.name: outcome
ExplainOutcomeParam.description: Keep rules that decided one of these outcomes.

AlertCursorParam.name: cursor
AlertCursorParam.description: Opaque keyset-pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor. When present, switches to cursor pagination (offset is ignored and total is omitted from the response) — avoids the OFFSET-scan cost of paging deep into a large result set.

AlertEventStatusParam.name: event_status
AlertEventStatusParam.description: Filters by the current workflow status of the alert's triggering event (tenant/template-defined, not a fixed enum).

AlertIdentifierParam.name: identifier
AlertIdentifierParam.description: Case-insensitive substring search against the values of the entity identifiers configured on the alert's template (e.g. account number, email). Requires at least 2 characters.

ScreeningTriggerParam.name: trigger
ScreeningTriggerParam.description: Filter to runs started by this trigger (manual, rule, scheduled, ...).

ScreeningTopicParam.name: topic
ScreeningTopicParam.description: Filter to runs whose requested topics include this code (e.g. sanction, role.pep).

ScreeningCountryParam.name: country
ScreeningCountryParam.description: Filter to runs with at least one non-filtered match in this country, matched against the match's country/nationality/jurisdiction/citizenship (ISO-3166 alpha-2, case-insensitive).

ScreeningDateFromParam.name: date_from
ScreeningDateFromParam.description: Only runs executed (ran on) at or after this time.

ScreeningDateToParam.name: date_to
ScreeningDateToParam.description: Only runs executed (ran on) at or before this time.
